title: Research
text: How does the developing visual cortex arrive at reliable representations of the outside world? Before eye opening, cortical networks already show structured spontaneous activity. After eye opening, visual experience reshapes this endogenous activity into representations that respond consistently to the same stimulus. My research asks which circuit mechanisms carry this transition.

title: Research
text:
Emergence of reliable cortical representations
At eye opening, responses of ferret visual cortex to the same stimulus vary strongly from trial to trial. Over the following days they become reliable. Combining chronic two-photon imaging with recurrent network models, we found that this reliability arises when visual input becomes aligned with the endogenous network structure, rather than from a general reduction of noise. See Trägenap et al., Nature Neuroscience 2025.

title: Research
text:
Feedforward input and recurrent circuits
How do feedforward inputs interact with recurrent cortical circuits during development? Together with the Fitzpatrick lab we showed that coherent cortical responses develop as feedforward inputs become more discriminable and better aligned with the recurrent network. See Lempel, Trägenap et al., Neuron 2025.

title: Research
text:
Millimetre-scale selective amplification
With the Smith lab we study how the developing cortex selectively amplifies particular activity patterns across millimetres of cortical surface, and which network properties can account for this. See Mulholland, Trägenap et al., bioRxiv 2026 (co-first authors).

title: Research
text:
Methods
Dynamical recurrent network models, analysis of large-scale calcium imaging data, and the comparison of model predictions with chronically recorded neural populations. Research code is on GitHub.

title: Sigrid Trägenap
text:
I am a computational neuroscientist at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies (FIAS) and Goethe University Frankfurt, working in the group of Matthias Kaschube.
I study how reliable sensory representations emerge during the development of the visual cortex. To do this I combine dynamical recurrent network models of cortical circuits with the analysis of chronic two-photon calcium imaging data from ferret visual cortex, recorded in long-standing collaborations with the labs of David Fitzpatrick (Max Planck Florida Institute for Neuroscience) and Gordon Smith (University of Minnesota).
I submitted my PhD thesis, Emergence of reliable sensory representations in cortical development, in January 2026.
